title: Streaming checkpoint handshake and incremental chunk validation for SSE
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Clients experience partial responses and duplicate side-effects when network flaps during long-running streamed generations (function calls, tool invocations, and structured JSON output). Current SSE semantics at Redwood do not provide a compact, backward-compatible handshake for reconnect that: 1) expresses the last fully-committed application-visible event boundary, 2) verifies chunk integrity to avoid duplicate apply semantics, and 3) negotiates fallback to older event encodings for legacy SDKs.

Goal: Implement a streaming reconnect handshake and per-chunk incremental validation scheme for our SSE endpoint that: (a) uses a light-weight checkpoint token (sequence id + 8-byte checksum) that clients can persist and send on reconnect, (b) defines a clear commit rule for function/tool call boundaries (only consider a function call committed when the closing structured object is fully received and checksum-validated), and (c) provides a compatibility negotiation bit in the handshake so older clients can fall back to line-based JSONL framing.

Non-goal: This ticket does not change transport (we will keep SSE over HTTP/1.x for hosted API). It does not implement TLS/KMS changes or RBAC policy surface areas.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server generates checkpoint tokens for each committed output boundary and exposes them in SSE comment lines using the header prefix ': ckpt='. 2) On reconnect, server accepts client-supplied last_seen tokens and resumes from the next sequence, rejecting mismatches with a clear 409-like event (event: resume-error) containing diagnostic fields. 3) Function/tool-call outputs are never emitted as committed until their closing token and checksum are validated. 4) Backwards compatibility: when client includes 'Accept-Stream-Compat: jsonl-v1' header, server falls back to legacy JSONL framing without checksum but still includes sequence numbers. 5) Integration tests simulate mid-response disconnects with randomized chunk drops and assert exactly-once semantic for function calls and zero corruption for structured outputs. 6) SDK patches for Node/Python are prepared and linked in PRs before rollout to staging.
design_decisions:
- Checkpoint token format chosen as 'seq:<number>|chk:<hex8>' to keep token length small and human-readable for debugging.
- Use CRC32C truncated to 8 hex characters as per-chunk checksum for speed in the serving runtime and C++/Rust libraries.
- Sequence numbers are per-stream monotonic event counters (not byte offsets) to make reassembly simple across protocol variants.
- Commitment rule: only after we emit a special 'event: committed' SSE comment with the checkpoint token do we mark application-visible side-effects as durable. This avoids double-invoke on resume.
- Backoff: clients should use exponential backoff with full jitter starting at 100ms up to 3s; server may include 'retry' SSE comment to adjust.
- Compatibility: feature negotiated via header 'Accept-Stream-Proto' and server-side feature gate. This keeps the runtime code path small and allows progressive rollout to Dedicated/Private with a config flag.

Trade-offs considered: checksum vs HMAC for integrity. We chose checksum for performance and size; HMAC was rejected because we don't want key management burden for short-lived stream checkpoints and because server-side authoritative state prevents deliberate tampering being a priority for this iteration.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge server-side feature-flagged implementation behind 'stream-checkpoints' flag. 2) Publish SDK patches (Node v0.24.3, Python v0.17.1) that understand and persist checkpoint tokens; release to npm/pypi with experimental tag. 3) Enable feature for 10% of hosted traffic in Canary (metrics: resumed-success-rate, duplicate-function-call-rate, mean-latency-of-resume). 4) If canary stable for 72h, increase to 50% then 100%. 5) Day-0 mitigation: admin toggle to disable checkpoint emission per-tenant. 6) Coordinate with Dedicated on a minor agent update for the config flag. Estimated total rollout: 2 weeks.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for checksum generation/validation.
- Integration harness that replays recorded streams and injects TCP drops at specific offsets and asserts last-seen token semantics.
- Fuzz test that feeds randomized chunk splits to parser and ensures structured outputs are always valid JSON and function call objects are either fully present or not applied.
- End-to-end tests with SDKs that simulate client reconnects (graceful and abrupt) and verify idempotency for example function that increments a counter (should not double-increment).
- Observability: add metrics 'stream.resume.attempts', 'stream.resume.success', 'stream.duplicate.function_calls'.
- QA matrix: hosted, dedicated, and private (on-prem) smoke tests.
comments: 2026-03-02 | Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes - agreed to sequence+checksum token format. Action items: Diego to prototype server emission and Sara to draft SDK change set.

2026-03-04 | Diego Morales: Early prototype emits ': ckpt=seq:42|chk:3f2a1b7c' comments after each committed boundary. Found parser edge-case when chunk boundary splits inside UTF-8 multibyte sequence; added defensive reassembly. PR opened: 3921.

2026-03-06 | Sara Liu: Node SDK patch saves last checkpoint to in-memory retry store and sends 'Last-Checkpoint' header on reconnect. Need to add persistent store option in next cycle. Code review feedback: avoid blocking disk writes on main event loop (suggested background flush).

2026-03-08 | QA (Marco): Integration harness injected random disconnects, saw 0.6% duplicate function calls in canary config when the server emitted checkpoint immediately after function close — root cause: race where client ack arrived after server closed connection. Mitigation: server will delay emission until function close is fully flushed to socket or include higher granularity 'pending' state in token.
